module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 163

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/163](https://www.erdosproblems.com/163)
- [BuEr75] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P., On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio.
  Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai (1975).
- [Le17] Lee, C., Ramsey numbers of degenerate graphs. Ann. of Math. (2) 185 (2017), 791-829.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos163

/--
The Burr-Erdős conjecture: For any $d\geq 1$ if $H$ is a graph such that every subgraph
contains a vertex of degree at most $d$ then
$$R(H)\ll_d n.$$

Solved by Lee [Le17], who proved that $R(H) \leq 2^{2^{O(d)}}n$.

This problem is #9 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

The linked formal proof (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol) gives, for graphs `H` on `Fin n`, a natural
constant `C ≥ 1` with `RamseyFor H (C * n)` (every red/blue colouring of `K_{C n}` contains a
monochromatic copy of `H`); transporting along `Fintype.equivFin` gives the statement below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos163.lean#L53"]
theorem erdos_163 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d →
      ∃ C > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (H : SimpleGraph V),
        H.IsDegenerate d →
        (SimpleGraph.diagonalGraphRamsey H : ℝ) ≤ C * Fintype.card V := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos163

findings.description: The module docstring's reference list gives the wrong title for the Burr–Erdős source paper: "[BuEr75] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P., On the Ramsey number of graphs with small degree-ratio. Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai (1975)." No Burr–Erdős paper has this title. The 1975 Colloq. Math. Soc. János Bolyai paper in which Burr and Erdős posed the conjecture is "On the magnitude of generalized Ramsey numbers for graphs". The venue and year in the file match that paper; only the title is invented. The mathematics of `erdos_163` is unaffected.

reformulations.difference: The source's hypothesis, "every subgraph contains a vertex of degree at most d", is encoded by `SimpleGraph.IsDegenerate d`. That predicate says every nonempty `Finset` s of vertices contains a v with at most d neighbours inside s. So it quantifies only over induced subgraphs, with degrees counted in H[s].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Induced subgraphs are subgraphs, so the source's condition implies `IsDegenerate`. Conversely, take any subgraph G' with nonempty vertex set s, and let v ∈ s be the vertex that `IsDegenerate` provides. Every G'-edge at v is an H-edge to a vertex of s, so deg_{G'}(v) ≤ |N_H(v) ∩ s| ≤ d. Proved in Lean for finite V: `H.IsDegenerate d ↔ ∀ G' : H.Subgraph, G'.verts.Nonempty → G'.verts.Finite → ∃ v ∈ G'.verts, (G'.neighborSet v).ncard ≤ d`, using `(⊤ : H.Subgraph).induce ↑s` for one direction and `G'.verts.toFinset` for the other.

reformulations.difference: The source's "R(H) ≪_d n" (n the number of vertices of H) becomes a uniform bound `diagonalGraphRamsey H ≤ C * Fintype.card V`. It is required for every finite vertex type `V : Type`, including empty and small ones, with one real `C > 0` depending only on d. The whole claim is wrapped as `answer(True) ↔ …` although the source states an assertion, not a question.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite graph is isomorphic to one on `Fin n : Type`, and `graphRamsey` is invariant under isomorphism, so restricting to universe 0 loses nothing. Suppose the bound holds only for n ≥ N₀. There are finitely many isomorphism classes of graphs on fewer than N₀ vertices, each with a finite value (sInf of a set that Ramsey's theorem makes nonempty). Enlarging C therefore gives a uniform bound for n ≥ 1. For n = 0 the value is 0 ≤ C·0; I checked in Lean that `diagonalGraphRamsey` is 0 on `Fin 0`. `C > 0` is forced anyway, since R(H) ≥ |V| ≥ 1 for nonempty V; I checked in Lean that every n in the defining set is ≥ card V, and that R(K₂) = 2. `answer(True) ↔ P` elaborates to `True ↔ P`, which is just P.

review.notes: The statement itself is faithful. `Erdos163.erdos_163` elaborates to `True ↔ ∀ d, 1 ≤ d → ∃ C > 0, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (H : SimpleGraph V), H.IsDegenerate d → ↑H.diagonalGraphRamsey ≤ C * ↑(Fintype.card V)`. This matches erdosproblems.com/163 ('For any d≥1 if H is a graph such that every subgraph contains a vertex of degree at most d then R(H) ≪_d n', marked PROVED, Lee 2017). It also matches the graphs problem collection version and Lee's formulation. `graphRamsey` is the usual sInf over n such that every 2-colouring (C, Cᶜ) of Fin n contains a copy of H; `IsContained` means a not-necessarily-induced copy, which is the right notion. Ramsey's theorem makes the set nonempty, so the `sInf ∅ = 0` default is never reached. Checks compiled in /workspace/review: R = 0 on Fin 0; R(K₂) = 2; every n in the defining set is ≥ card V; K₃ is 2-degenerate but not 1-degenerate; `IsDegenerate` is equivalent to the source's 'every subgraph' condition. Category `research solved` and `answer(True)` agree with the source, so there are no status issues. On the formal_proof record, the link points at line 53, which is `theorem erdos_163 :`. That theorem states `∀ d ≥ 1, ∃ C : ℕ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ n (H : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), IsDegenerateAtMost H d → RamseyFor H (C * n)`. Its definitions match FC's `IsDegenerate` and `graphRamsey` set. I copied those definitions, replacing `HasCopy` with Mathlib's equivalent `IsContained`, and proved in Lean that this statement implies the FC right-hand side, transporting along `Fintype.equivFin`. So the docstring's description of the proof is accurate. A grep of its 39 modules (~16k lines) found no `sorry`, `axiom`, `admit` or `native_decide`; I did not compile it (it targets Lean/Mathlib v4.33.0). Not defects, for context only: the source's variants are not formalized (the file has a TODO). These are the equivalent arboricity and average-degree forms and the still-open conjecture R(H) ≤ 2^{O(d)} n. Style points such as the `answer(True) ↔` wrapper on a non-question and the proof note in the docstring are also not misformalizations.
